---
title: "Tenant-Service Record Keeping in Toronto: Low Ratings Are More Common in Smaller Apartment Buildings"
author: 
  - Kexin Liu
thanks: "Code and data are available at: [https://github.com/cocoUofT/Apartment_Evaluation](https://github.com/cocoUofT/Apartment_Evaluation])."
date: 27 September 2026
date-format: long
abstract: "Tenant service records track reported problems and managers’ responses, helping ensure accountability in rental housing. This paper uses Toronto’s apartment-building evaluations from 2023 to September 2026 to study tenant-service-log ratings, their patterns across different building sizes, how they change over time, and differences across wards relative to benchmarks based on building-size composition. We found that, among buildings with an available rating at their latest evaluation, 14.0% of buildings with 10–19 units had incomplete or outdated tenant service logs, whereas only 1.1% of buildings with 100 or more units had incomplete logs. These differences show where further investigation of record-keeping practices may be useful, although the causes and whether tenants’ problems were resolved promptly remain unclear from the log scores alone."
format: pdf
number-sections: true
bibliography: references.bib
